body:
_Migrated from issue #1390, filed 2026-08-05._

Reported by @jrodrigoferreira on #324 against v4.1.29, with a full reproduction. Split out because it is atomic and independently shippable, where #324 is the three-way-sync umbrella.

**Symptom.** Read a book to 80% in the browser, then sync a Kobo that is still at 70%, and the library drops back to 70%. The position you actually resume from stays at 80%, so the two carriers disagree and the displayed number goes backwards. Progress the user made is silently lost from the display.

**Cause.** `cps/kobo.py:1544`, in `HandleStateRequest`:

```python
current_bookmark.progress_percent = request_bookmark["ProgressPercent"]
current_bookmark.content_source_progress_percent = request_bookmark["ContentSourceProgressPercent"]
```

Both writes are unconditional. Nothing compares the incoming percentage against what is stored, so any device that is behind overwrites a further position on every sync.

The browser writer already has exactly the guard this path is missing. `record_web_reader_progress` (`cps/services/reading_position.py`) refuses a percentage at or below the stored one, and its docstring states the policy as **furthest wins**, describing it as "matching the rule KOSync already applies across devices". The policy is real and documented; it is simply not enforced on the device writer. One of the two writers honours it and the other does not, which is why this only shows up once both are in use — and v4.1.29 is what put both in use.

**Second defect in the same handler.** `g.kobo_reading_state_lm` is set from the device's own `LastModified` (`kobo.py:1538`) and `receive_before_flush` (`cps/ub.py:1131`) writes it to `kobo_reading_state.last_modified`. A device clock behind the server therefore moves the row's timestamp backwards. The sync feed decides what to deliver with `kobo_reading_state.last_modified > sync_token.reading_state_last_modified` (`kobo.py:544`), so a regressed timestamp can also suppress delivery of a change that really happened — consistent with the reporter's second symptom, that the browser's 80% never reached the device at all.

**Confidence.** The unconditional overwrite is certain from source. The delivery-suppression half is inference from the same code path and is not yet reproduced against a device; it needs runtime confirmation before being claimed fixed.

**Scope note.** This is *not* #1345. That issue covers the read-**status** carriers (`ReadBook.read_status` vs the configured column) and cites `kobo.py:1575`; this is the progress **percentage** at `kobo.py:1544`. Same shape — several writers, no shared policy — different data and different line. They should be fixed with the same primitive, not folded into one another.

**Fix shape.** Give the device writer the same furthest-wins check, and stop `last_modified` regressing. Note the honest limit `record_web_reader_progress` already documents about itself: acceptance decided in Python rather than in the UPDATE is not proof against two writers racing. Doing this properly means one shared conditional-UPDATE primitive — accept in the `WHERE` clause, check the affected-row count — used by *both* writers so they cannot drift. Writing a second Python-side check would repair this report while leaving the class open.

**Regression test must cover:** stored 80 + device 70 → stays 80; stored 70 + device 80 → becomes 80; a device `LastModified` older than the stored one must not move the row's timestamp backwards.
title: Kobo sync overwrites a further reading position with a device's older one (progress goes backwards)
